correctness.rationale: Independence forbids two vertices in one column, forces opposite rows for adjacent selected columns. Three consecutive occupied columns necessarily alternate and give the vertex opposite their middle a forbidden third selected neighbor; conversely forbidding cyclic 111 prevents any vertex having three selected neighbors. Every occupied run length 1 or 2 has exactly two row choices. For k selected columns and r runs, count length-two runs binom(r,k−r), positive empty-column gaps binom(n−k−1,r−1), starting positions n/r and row assignments 2^r. Summing cyclic 3-window inequalities gives 3k≤2n and construction attains floor(2n/3); substitution yields all extremal counts. Fresh direct labelled-graph enumeration for n=3..10 checked coefficients independently, including seams and n=3.
